required_propositions.claim: A finite determination destroys itself because the precise form of its failure dictates the determinate successor.
Logical categories, phenomenological shapes and historical institutions develop through distinct registers that cannot substitute for one another.
Absolute Idealism preserves nature and finite minds as real moments while rejecting perception-dependence, a second world and a cosmic person.
Recognition becomes relational and historical without replacing the larger system, while the lord loses the reason for victory.
Eurocentric teleology rationalises victors unless qualified, while Objective Spirit locates freedom through right, morality and ethical life.
The qualified conclusion preserves Hegelian achievements while retrospective necessity, sheer existence and particular irreducibility remain costs.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 14/55 — The worked case - Being, Nothing and Becoming (continued)

propositions.claim: Dasein differs from Wirklichkeit because rational actuality cannot mean that whatever exists is right.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 15/55 — Four misreadings of the first triad, blocked - and the honest limit

propositions.claim: The first triad illustrates method without proving the system because the move from indistinguishability to transition remains contested.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 16/55 — Abstract versus concrete universal, and the whole quotation

propositions.claim: The concrete universal preserves differentiated instances through self-particularisation while truth includes the process of becoming whole.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 17/55 — Identity-in-difference and the three moments of the Concept

propositions.claim: Identity-in-difference preserves determinate difference while the Concept unites universality, particularity and individuality.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 18/55 — The bad infinite, the true infinite, and the architecture they force

propositions.claim: The bad infinite remains limited because it excludes the finite while true infinity includes self-limitation and return.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 19/55 — The bad infinite, the true infinite, and the architecture they force (continued)

propositions.claim: Conceptual self-comprehension does not make each finite philosopher omniscient because the claimed standpoint exceeds individual knowledge.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 20/55 — The three forms of Spirit, and ethical life at owned depth

propositions.claim: Subjective, Objective and Absolute Spirit distinguish agency, institutions and self-comprehension while ethical life organises family, civil society and state.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 21/55 — The three forms of Spirit, and ethical life at owned depth (continued)

propositions.claim: Spirit depends on human culture and action without becoming a ghost, cosmic person or devotional synonym for God.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 22/55 — Absolute Idealism - statement, four denials and the interpretive control

propositions.claim: Absolute Idealism preserves nature and finite minds as real moments while rejecting perception-dependence, a second world and a cosmic person.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 23/55 — Absolute Idealism - statement, four denials and the interpretive control (continued)

propositions.claim: Interpretive control requires noting the metaphysical split in one clause without adjudicating it inside an exam script.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 24/55 — Substance and Subject, and the actuality discrimination

propositions.claim: Substance becomes Subject through self-differentiation and return while Wirklichkeit distinguishes realised concept from bare Dasein.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 25/55 — Substance and Subject, and the actuality discrimination (continued)

propositions.claim: The actuality distinction permits institutional criticism while it does not erase conservative applications of Hegelian politics.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 26/55 — The three prongs against Kant's thing in itself

propositions.claim: Hegel challenges Kant because relational limits, empty abstraction and fixed dualism undermine an external noumenal remainder.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 27/55 — The three prongs against Kant's thing in itself (continued)

propositions.claim: The limit argument rejects an external remainder without proving system completeness or positive knowledge of the thing-in-itself.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 28/55 — Kant's reply, the verdict grid, and the reality of the phenomenal world

propositions.claim: Kantian negative noumenon restricts categories while the verdict varies across two-world, affection and limiting-concept readings.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 29/55 — Kant's reply, the verdict grid, and the reality of the phenomenal world (continued)

propositions.claim: Phenomenal reality requires mediation and finite-infinite overcoming rather than Berkeleyan subjectivity or a mechanical triad.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 30/55 — Lordship and bondage - the four steps and the reversal

propositions.claim: Recognition struggle yields lord and bondsman roles while the lord depends and the bondsman self-forms through fear, service and labour.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 31/55 — Lordship and bondage - the four steps and the reversal (continued)

propositions.claim: Lordship reversal is dialectical because the lord receives the self-defeating recognition that he requested.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 32/55 — The explicit limit, the reception firewall and the register note

propositions.claim: The episode destabilises domination without final recognition while later receptions must remain distinct from Hegelian text and logical register.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 33/55 — The explicit limit, the reception firewall and the register note (continued)

propositions.claim: Recognition becomes relational and historical without replacing the larger system, while the lord loses the reason for victory.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 34/55 — Stoicism, Scepticism and the unhappy consciousness - the three failures

propositions.claim: Stoicism becomes empty, Scepticism becomes performatively contradictory and Unhappy Consciousness internalises division because each shape fails its criterion.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 35/55 — Stoicism, Scepticism and the unhappy consciousness - the three failures (continued)

propositions.claim: Unhappy Consciousness cannot abandon either Unchangeable or Changeable while its printed subterms specify the internal split.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 36/55 — The four moments, the reversal into Reason, and the objection ledger

propositions.claim: Devotion, work and the mediator culminate in universality because complete renunciation reverses into Reason.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 37/55 — The four moments, the reversal into Reason, and the objection ledger (continued)

propositions.claim: Kierkegaardian, theological and analytic objections leave distinct residuals while Feuerbach and Marx transform rather than reproduce Hegel.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 38/55 — The Logic-to-Nature seam - the dilemma and Hegel's own text

propositions.claim: The Logic-to-Nature seam asks how categories yield existent Nature while free release names a non-temporal structural externality.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 39/55 — The Logic-to-Nature seam - the dilemma and Hegel's own text (continued)

propositions.claim: Nature becomes contingent because its impotence prevents the Concept from holding fast and rejects deduction of natural particulars.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 40/55 — The four standing objections to the seam, with replies and residuals

propositions.claim: Schelling, Feuerbach, Trendelenburg and analytic critics challenge existence, theology, motion and personification while every reply leaves a residual.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 41/55 — The four standing objections to the seam, with replies and residuals (continued)

propositions.claim: Reflexive transition avoids a deciding agent while the metaphor remains incomplete and post-Hegelian heirs retain different sides.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 42/55 — Dialectic in history - source status, mechanism and schema

propositions.claim: Historical dialectic requires posthumous source caution and immanent mechanism before the one-some-all civilisational schema.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 43/55 — Dialectic in history - source status, mechanism and schema (continued)

propositions.claim: The cunning of reason explains consequences beyond intentions while the civilisation list only illustrates the prior mechanism.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 44/55 — The required criticism, Popper, and where freedom is supposed to land

propositions.claim: Eurocentric teleology rationalises victors unless qualified, while Objective Spirit locates freedom through right, morality and ethical life.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 45/55 — The required criticism, Popper, and where freedom is supposed to land (continued)

propositions.claim: Art and religion remain optional because philosophy conceptually comprehends their shared content at the owned depth.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 46/55 — Comparison matrix - Kant, Hegel, Marx, Kierkegaard

propositions.claim: Criterion-led comparison distinguishes Kant, Hegel, Marx and Kierkegaard through noumenon, reality, dialectic, freedom and truth.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 47/55 — Comparison matrix - Kant, Hegel, Marx, Kierkegaard (continued)

propositions.claim: Marx transforms dialectic into material relations while Kierkegaard rejects the system for the existing individual.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 48/55 — Hegel against Berkeley - the 2024 axis, and the optional Strawson bridge

propositions.claim: Berkeleyan ideas, spirits and God differ because Hegel treats nature and finite Spirit as moments of a developing whole.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 49/55 — Hegel against Berkeley - the 2024 axis, and the optional Strawson bridge (continued)

propositions.claim: Strawson and Hegel reject a causalised noumenon while their remedies diverge into mediation and descriptive metaphysics.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 50/55 — The criticism ledger and the directive decoder

propositions.claim: Critical assessment requires criticism, reply and residual because a one-sided objection forfeits philosophical judgement.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 51/55 — The criticism ledger and the directive decoder (continued)

propositions.claim: Directive control requires technical terms, fixed axes and explained transitions while rejecting parallel summaries and stage lists.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 52/55 — PYQ routes 2018-2025, the answer spine and the graded verdict bank

propositions.claim: Verified PYQ routes connect method, phenomenal reality, history and Kant through distinct answer spines and ownership boundaries.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 53/55 — PYQ routes 2018-2025, the answer spine and the graded verdict bank (continued)

propositions.claim: The universal answer spine requires transition, text, critic and residual while mark scaling changes the architecture.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 54/55 — Trap sheet, provenance rules and the qualified conclusion

propositions.claim: The trap sheet preserves provenance and close distinctions because triadic shorthand, Wirklichkeit, Geist, Berkeley, history and Nature invite recurring errors.

destination_anchors.anchor: FORMAL PANEL 55/55 — Trap sheet, provenance rules and the qualified conclusion (continued)

propositions.claim: The qualified conclusion preserves Hegelian achievements while retrospective necessity, sheer existence and particular irreducibility remain costs.
